title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's notice, including their different rollout descriptions. The documented controls and background licensing are supported, and the page appropriately leaves the new group report's undocumented requirements and controls unresolved.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationales
claims.claim: The notice describes an optional administrative report, not an automatic change to group or site permissions.
claims.quote: SharePoint administrators will be able to use the new report to identify all sites accessible to a given group. The report will show the extent of the group's access to those sites.

claims.claim: The new group report's default state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint group report default role limits; data access governance group report default CSV. Read the supplied roadmap and notice, DAG overview, PowerShell guide and Start/Get references; none states a default for this report.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Report-specific licensing for the new arbitrary-group report is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint group permissions report license; data access governance group report licensing; 561039. Read DAG overview, SAM prerequisites and Start reference; these give general prerequisites, not this new report's entitlement.

claims.claim: No price is published for the new group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance report given group licensing price meter role default enabled snapshot limits CSV. Opened DAG overview, SAM prerequisites and PowerShell guide; no group-report price was found.

claims.claim: No meter is published for the new group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance report given group licensing price meter role default enabled snapshot limits CSV. Opened DAG overview, SAM prerequisites and PowerShell guide; no group-report meter was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet document the exact arbitrary-group report UI or a PowerShell command or parameter set for it.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance permission report given group create report PowerShell group permissions; SharePoint given group report. Read DAG overview, user-report page, PowerShell guide and Start/Get references; only other reports were documented.

claims.claim: The Data access governance overview does not describe the new report for an arbitrary given group.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint given group report; 561039. Read the full DAG overview: it describes users and the special Everyone/EEEU reports, but not the new arbitrary-group report described by this roadmap item.

claims.claim: The existing site permissions for users report lists all sites accessible to specified users rather than taking an arbitrary group as its input.
claims.quote: This report lists all sites a user can access

claims.claim: The user report distinguishes entire-site access from access to specific sections.
claims.quote: helps admins determine whether they can access the entire site or specific sections

claims.claim: The user report includes direct access and indirect access through groups.
claims.quote: granted directly to the user or indirectly through groups.

claims.claim: The existing user report can be downloaded as CSV.
claims.quote: Select Download report for the selected user option to download the report as a CSV file.

claims.claim: The new group report's output format is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: data access governance group report default CSV; SharePoint given group report. Read DAG overview, user-report page and PowerShell guide; CSV descriptions concern other reports, not the new arbitrary-group report.

claims.claim: Learn warns that DAG reports might not work when nonpseudonymized report data is selected.
claims.quote: Reports might not work if you select nonpseudonymized report data for your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing that Reports setting requires a Global Administrator.
claims.quote: To change this setting, you must be a Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to the Microsoft 365 admin center Reports setting and to clear Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Go to the Reports setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and clear Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn presents Restricted access control as a follow-up remediation option for DAG findings, not as the group report itself.
claims.quote:
Remedial actions from Data access governance reports
For immediate action:
Use Restricted access control (RAC) to limit access to a specific group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn presents the Change history report as a follow-up investigation option for DAG findings.
claims.quote: Review the 'Change history' report to identify recent permission changes that might have led to oversharing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn presents Site access review as a follow-up remediation option for DAG findings.
claims.quote: Use the Site access review feature to request that site owners review and update permissions.

claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites identify SharePoint Administrator as an administrative role.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrator: Provides full administrative control over the SharePoint Online service, including sites, policies, groups, and operational tasks

claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites identify SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator as having wider governance capabilities including viewing content metadata.
claims.quote:
SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator: Includes all SharePoint Administrator capabilities, plus advanced governance capabilities such as:
Viewing metadata (names, paths, URLs) across SharePoint content

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not yet specify the formal role requirement for the new arbitrary-group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint group report default role limits; SharePoint given group report. Read SAM prerequisites, DAG overview and PowerShell guide; the special Everyone/EEEU report has a role requirement, but the new arbitrary-group report is not covered.

claims.claim: The user report captures data from up to 48 hours before generation.
claims.quote: Reports capture data from up to 48 hours before generation.

claims.claim: The user report has a limit of five reports.
claims.quote: You can have up to five reports.

claims.claim: The user reports can be run again every 30 days.
claims.quote: You can run reports again every 30 days.

claims.claim: Whether the new group report shares the user report's freshness, count and rerun limits is undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint group report default role limits; SharePoint data access governance report given group licensing price meter role default enabled snapshot limits CSV. Read DAG overview, user-report page and PowerShell guide; no new-group-report limits found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The general DAG reports page directs readers to the SAM prerequisites.
claims.quote:
What you need to create a data access governance report

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites list at least one user assigned a Microsoft Copilot licence as one route to SAM capabilities.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. (The user doesn't need to be a SharePoint administrator.)

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A SharePoint K, P1 or P2 subscription plus the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on is another route.
claims.quote: Your subscription includes SharePoint K, P1, or P2, and your organization purchases the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 is another listed route to SAM capabilities.
claims.quote: Your organization has Microsoft 365 E7, also known as The Frontier Suite.

claims.claim: SAM requires a listed base subscription: Office 365 E3/E5/A5, Microsoft 365 E1/E3/E5/A5, or Microsoft 365 GCC/GCC-High/DoD.
claims.quote:
Your organization must have one of the following base licenses:
Office 365 E3, E5, or A5
Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5, or A5
Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High, or DoD

claims.claim: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access DAG reporting.
claims.quote: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access Data access governance reporting

claims.claim: That E5 reporting entitlement does not permit viewing or using the other SAM features.
claims.quote: but can't view or use the other SharePoint Advanced Management features.

claims.claim: The E5-only reporting entitlement does not provide snapshot reports.
claims.quote: The reports don't provide snapshot reports or remedial actions.

claims.claim: The E5-only reporting entitlement does not provide remedial actions.
claims.quote: The reports don't provide snapshot reports or remedial actions.

claims.claim: Learn says DAG reports are unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet even with the required licences.
claims.quote: The reports are currently unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet, even if you have the required licenses.

claims.claim: The general DAG reports path is SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center ... In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity> lists existing DAG reports without establishing support for the new group report.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center.
Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    [-Workload <WorkloadEnum>]
    [-ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>]

claims.claim: From Reports > Data access governance, the user-report creation path is Site permissions for users > View reports > Create report.
claims.quote:
From the Data access governance landing page, select View reports under Site permissions for users.
Select Create report to generate your report.

claims.claim: The listed Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight call uses valid user-report parameters, the documented PermissionsReport/Snapshot/SharePoint values and the reference spelling UserPrincipalNames.
claims.quote:
UserPermissionsParameterSet
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    -Workload <WorkloadEnum>
    -ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>
    -Name <String>
    -UserPrincipalNames <System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.String]>

claims.claim: The Start reference includes PermissionedUsers and PermissionsReport among ReportEntity values.
claims.quote: Accepted values: | Everyone, EveryoneExceptExternalUsers, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems, PermissionedUsers, PermissionsReport, SensitivityLabelForFiles, SharingLinks_Anyone, SharingLinks_Guests, SharingLinks_PeopleInYourOrg

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide uses UserEmailList where the cmdlet reference uses UserPrincipalNames.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name "UserSharePointReport" -UserEmailList "a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide says UserEmailList requires user principal names.
claims.quote: While the parameter is named UserEmailList, the report requires user principal names.

claims.claim: Learn requires generating the site permissions for your organization report at least once before the user report.
claims.quote:
Review these important details before creating your first report:
Make sure that the site permissions for your organization report is generated at least once.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not yet classified this new arbitrary-group report as a snapshot report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance report given group licensing price meter role default enabled snapshot limits CSV; SharePoint given group report. Read DAG overview and PowerShell guide; their snapshot classifications cover other reports.

claims.claim: Learn instructs readers to use their organization's SharePoint administrator credentials to access DAG reports.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center with the SharePoint administrator credentials for your organization.
